blocks.title: Utilities on live streets and occupied sites.
blocks.body:
We install and upgrade sanitary sewers, storm sewers and watermains, with the manholes, catch basins, service connections and hydrants that go with them. Much of this work happens on live residential streets and around occupied schools, so we plan traffic, access and service connections to keep residents and businesses running while the work goes on.

On the [Western Crescent and Kingston Road sewer separation](projects/kingston-road-sewer-separation.html) for the University Endowment Lands we hold the prime contract: twelve new precast manholes, fifteen properties reconnected, seven new catch basins, and new sanitary and storm mains from 250 to 450 mm, with CCTV inspection and pressure testing before handover.

blocks.title: Water services for new buildings.
blocks.body: Onsite and offsite fire and domestic water upgrades are part of most of our school and development projects, including [Guildford Park Secondary](projects/guildford-park-secondary.html), [Queen Elizabeth Elementary](projects/queen-elizabeth-elementary.html), [Parkcrest Elementary](projects/parkcrest-elementary.html) and [James Whiteside Elementary](projects/james-whiteside-elementary.html).

items.a: Yes. On [Kingston Road](projects/kingston-road-sewer-separation.html) we replaced a combined sewer with new sanitary and storm systems laid side by side, each with its own manholes, service connections and catch basins.

items.q: Do residents stay connected during the work?
items.a: Yes. New services are installed ahead of time and transferred over once the new mains are tested, so every property stays connected through the job.

items.q: Do you hold municipal prime contracts?
items.a: Yes. We hold the prime contract for the Kingston Road sewer separation for the University Endowment Lands, and our first prime contract with the City of Surrey was the [North Surrey utility improvements](projects/north-surrey-utility-improvements.html).

items.q: Do you test and inspect new mains?
items.a: Yes. CCTV inspection and pressure testing are part of our utility scope, along with abandonment of old manholes and as-built records.

blocks.title: Tendering utility work?
blocks.text: Send the drawings and tender documents. Our estimating team will respond within one business day.
